question: Past the wall (two maximal blocks sharing two points): does the roster engine equal the program's engine, and what do the partnered and sub-count bounds of Lemma 2 read of the next round of MERGE-BURST's 14 unread explosive starts?

public_inputs.run: scripts/longrun.py launch job.py; python3 -B merge.py <out dir> <results.json>
public_inputs.reused: runs/merge-burst (the 16 starts); runs/touch-census; REDUCE-BLOCKS hublib and sampler; joinlib engine; fastlib

forbidden_inputs: Changing a bound, the search, the sub-count procedure, a prediction or a threshold after reading the frozen run
cheapest_meaningful_control: start-00, the closed explosive start (followed to its close; its merge stage has one block)

predictions.B1: roster engine equals program engine wherever both finish
predictions.B2: start-03 double count; fastlib lists 28,064 round-8 groups, largest 109
predictions.B3: Lemma 2 bounds at most the listed groups at every stage
predictions.B5: >= 10 of 13 other unread starts: better bound at the last built stage exceeds its count
predictions.B6: no unread start reaches a one-block stage

decision_rules.each: held iff its condition in the pre-registration holds

stop_rule: One run; stop at the result.
runtime: about two to three hours on 2 workers (20 minutes per followed start at most)
disclosed_exploration: start-03 to round 8 with the compact engine; partnered sets on start-03's stages (4 restarts); the partnered start of order 3; smoke runs of A's machine check and of B's follow on start-00
